points: The October print will reveal whether aerospace demand stayed strong through the September-ending quarter; a revenue beat and raised guidance would create a long side, while a miss and cut would create a short side.
It will show if nonsegment expense growth is easing after rising 21.8% year-over-year in the last reported quarter; slower growth supports a long, re-acceleration supports a short.
Cash conversion will be tested after cash from operations fell 18% and free cash flow fell 28% in the last reported quarter; a rebound supports a long, continued weakness supports a short.
The print will update the FY2026/FY2027 EPS path that consensus already prices at $9.46 (+37.3%) and $10.73 (+13.5%); confirmation or a raise supports a long, a reduction supports a short.

Valuation is flagged fair versus the theme on a PEG of 0.9x median and P/E of 1.1x median, so the print must justify the growth premium; a beat does that for a long, a miss makes the multiple vulnerable for a short.
Reports suggest Woodward already beat and raised guidance in late July, so the October report will clarify whether that strength carried into the September-ending quarter or pulled forward demand.
watch: 90-day revenue estimate revision (rev90) moves above +0.50% with upward analyst revisions outpacing downgrades beyond the recent 8-up/1-down ratio — establishes
Q3 2026 revenue growth versus the prior-year quarter accelerates above the last reported +8% — supports a long; slows materially — supports a short.
FY2026 EPS guidance is raised or maintained at/above the $9.46 consensus — supports a long; cut — supports a short.
Free cash flow turns positive year-over-year after the last quarter’s -28% decline — supports a long; stays negative — supports a short.
Nonsegment expense growth slows from the last quarter’s +21.8% year-over-year — supports a long; re-accelerates — supports a short.
